predecessors.name: Kalmar Union
predecessors.text: the Danish and Norwegian realms of the Kalmar Union (Cliopatria: 2,947 of the 2,948 cells of the 1526 shape lie in the 1525 Kalmar Union shape)

ledger.x: 1526: Denmark and Norway stand as one realm under the Danish crown after Sweden left the Kalmar Union.
1537: the Norwegian riksråd is abolished and Norway is bound to Denmark in a dual monarchy.
1559: Frederick II buys the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek and Courland.
1563: war with Sweden.
13 December 1570: the Treaty of Stettin ends the war, 'Status quo ante bellum in Scandinavia'.
1572: Magnus's mainland lands in Estonia (Wiek, Pärnu, Rapla) pass to Russia in Cliopatria's draw.
1572: Courland's Pilten (Ventspils, Dundaga, Kuldiga) passes to Poland-Lithuania in Cliopatria's draw.
1595: Cliopatria extends Finnmark east to the Pasvik.
1611: Denmark-Norway attacks Sweden.
20 January 1613: the Treaty of Knäred.
January 1613: Denmark holds Älvsborg and Gullberg until the ransom is paid (infobox 'Älvsborg temporarily controlled by Denmark (1613)').
1619: the Älvsborg pledge ends.
1622: Cliopatria adds 5 cells on the lower Elbe (Hamburg 3, Niedersachsen 1, Schleswig-Holstein 1).
1625: Christian IV enters the Thirty Years' War in Lower Saxony.
September 1627: the Imperial armies invade Danish land.
22 May 1629: the Treaty of Lübeck.
22 May 1629: 'The treaty restored to Christian his pre-war possessions'; Holstein and Jutland are Danish again.
13 August 1645: the Treaty of Brömsebro ends the Torstenson War.
13 August 1645: Gotland and Ösel go to Sweden at Brömsebro.
13 August 1645: 'Sweden received the Danish province of Halland for a period of 30 years as a guarantee'.
1658: Denmark-Norway recognises the Gottorp dukes' sovereignty over their part of Schleswig.
February 1658: Charles X Gustav crosses the frozen belts.
26 February 1658 (8 March new style): the Treaty of Roskilde ends the Swedish hold on Zealand and leaves Denmark-Norway 'forced to give up a third of its territory to save the rest'.
1658: Scania and Blekinge are ceded.
1658: the Norwegian provinces of Bohuslän and Trøndelag are ceded.
1658: 'The immediate cession of the Danish province of Bornholm to Sweden.'
1660: the Treaty of Copenhagen.
1667: the County of Oldenburg comes under the Danish crown.
1712: Danish troops take Bremen-Verden from Sweden.
1713: Danish troops hold the Gottorp part of Schleswig.
1715: Denmark-Norway sells Bremen-Verden.
3 July 1720: the Treaty of Frederiksborg ends the Great Northern War for Denmark-Norway; 'Swedish support for Gottorp ceased'.
3 July 1720: 'Denmark also gained full control over Schleswig'; Sweden 'paid 600,000 Riksdaler in damages' and 'Danish-held areas of Swedish Pomerania were returned to Sweden'.
1773: the Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo.
1773: the ducal Holstein lands pass to the Danish crown in the same exchange.
1807: Cliopatria draws 3 cells (Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Syddanmark) as French.
1809: Cliopatria hands one Finnmark cell to the Russian Empire.
14 January 1814: Norway passes to the King of Sweden.
14 January 1814: Denmark-Norway ends at the Treaty of Kiel.

wars.name: Northern Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Stettin, 13 December 1570: 'Status quo ante bellum in Scandinavia'; Jämtland and Härjedalen returned, Älvsborg ransomed for 150,000 riksdaler, Swedish claims to Norway, Skåne, Halland, Blekinge and Gotland withdrawn.

wars.name: Kalmar War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Knäred, 20 January 1613: 'All conquests made by both sides are returned'; Sweden pays 1 million rixdollars for Älvsborg; free passage through the Sound.

wars.name: Danish phase of the Thirty Years' War (Emperor's War, Kejserkrigen)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Lübeck, 22 May 1629: pre-war possessions restored to Christian IV, who cedes his claims to Lower Saxon bishoprics.

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Brömsebro, 13 August 1645: Jämtland, Härjedalen, Gotland and Ösel ceded, Halland held for 30 years, Sweden exempt from the Sound Dues.

wars.name: Swedish invasion of Denmark-Norway (Treaties of Roskilde and Copenhagen)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Roskilde, 26 February 1658: a third of the realm ceded; Treaty of Copenhagen, 1660: Trøndelag and Bornholm restored.

wars.name: Great Northern War (Danish part)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Frederiksborg, 3 July 1720: Denmark gains full control over Schleswig, returns Danish-held Swedish Pomerania, Sweden pays 600,000 riksdaler.

certainty.note: The Norway-Sweden marches (Jämtland, Härjedalen, Lapland, Finnmark) and the Livonian holdings are approximate; the Sound and the Danish-German frontier on the Eider are not.

Province-by-province treaty cessions in 1645, 1658, 1660, 1720 and 1773 fix the lines; exceptions: Idre and Särna were 'not formally recognised until 1751', and the Arctic frontier in Finnmark stays soft.
